claims.claim_text: The indexed Groff Conklin is a high-confidence match to the author whom an official CIA history places with an OSS visual-artists group.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A CIA historical article names Groff Conklin among the artists working together in OSS and describes the group's wartime production.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact, highly distinctive full name appears both in the NARA OSS personnel index and in the official CIA account of an OSS work group. No conflicting Groff Conklin identity was found.
claims.temporal_assessment: The CIA source establishes wartime OSS context but neither an entry date nor a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: High confidence is used rather than confirmed because no unique private identifier or direct personnel-file link joins the two records.

claims.claim_text: Groff Conklin worked as a fiction editor and assistant manager at New York's Doubleday Bookstore early in his career.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Conklin began his career as an editor of fiction as an assistant manager at New York's Doubleday Bookstore.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Princeton's finding aid identifies Doubleday Bookstore as Conklin's workplace and describes his fiction-editing and assistant-manager functions.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The finding aid identifies a single Groff Conklin, dates him 1904-1968 and describes the same science-fiction author named in the CIA OSS history.
claims.temporal_assessment: The role is documented before World War II through career chronology and the finding aid's 1929-1934 context, but no exact employment dates or immediate pre-OSS sequence are supplied.
claims.match_notes: Published only as other documented pre-OSS employment. It is excluded from immediate-affiliation and last-civilian-employer counts.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index itself prints 'Agent Confidential' with the literal note 'no real n,' Box 138 and no name, rank or identifier. CIA, Library of Congress, Army, exact-phrase and archival searches cannot establish a lawful personal identity from the printed row. A newspaper classified-ad result using the words agent and confidential refers to no identified person and was rejected.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 138 to determine whether the deliberately anonymized row can be identified and published without overriding archival restrictions; preserve 'no real n' literally.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index supplies Eugene A Confrey, rank T-5, a literal seven-digit private identifier and Box 138. The Army file has Eugene A and Eugene F Confrey candidates but no identifier match; the exact-middle-initial row cannot be assigned by name alone. An official NIH search result mentioning a Eugene Confrey with wartime Army service remains discovery-only because the underlying document could not be inspected and no OSS or Box 138 bridge was established.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Resolve the literal seven-digit identifier and compare the Army and NIH leads against Box 138 before assigning any education, occupation or employer.
